notes: Step 1: two black 1x6 plates are placed side by side (arrows show them being brought together); they do not clutch each other until step 2.
Step 2: the white inverted 3x2 slope sits at one end of the two plates, bridging both. I assumed it covers the end 2 studs of each plate across both plates.
Page 2 also has a preview image and an FSC logo, which add no parts.
Step 3 is hard to read: I took it as the black 1x2 plate with handles on ends placed across the two black 1x6 plates at the left end.
Step 4: two light-gray 1x1 side-stud bricks (one per black plate) and an orange 2x2 plate. Exact positions and what each piece rests on are guesses.

Step 5 callout: a dark-gray bracket gets two silver round plates, built 2x (4 silver plates total). The two finished brackets are then attached at the front/left of the model. I guessed the bracket rests_on lists, and put the silver plates as side joins.
The bracket's silver plates are listed under rests_on of the bracket as a simplification; the real join is on the side face.

Step 6: the dark gray 2x2 pin brick goes on top at the left end, with its pin sticking out to the left (the propeller will probably go on it later). I assumed it rests on the two brackets' top plates.
Step 7: the orange 2x4 plate covers the pin brick and the orange 2x2 plate beside it. I guessed these are the pieces it rests on.
This is a new sub-assembly (wing and tail), separate from the fuselage built on pages 2-4. The fuselage is not yet joined to it.
Step 1: the two white 3x2 wedge plates are placed end to end and touch only through the tail shuttle added in step 2. Which wedge is left or right is my reading of the picture.
Step 2: the white tail shuttle (fin) sits on both wedges and bridges them.
Step 3: a black groove tile goes on each wedge next to the fin. A trans-green round plate goes on the left wedge tip and a trans-red one on the right tip. Which wedge each sits on is a guess.
Step 4: an orange 2x6 plate is pushed onto the underside of the wing/tail sub-assembly from page 5. The wedges are b16 and b17.

Step 8 (arrow): the sub-assembly with its orange plate is placed on top of the fuselage. The plate sits on the orange 2x4 plate b15 and the white inverted slope b3. The wing and tail end overhangs the rear.
Only one new piece is placed on this page, b23. I used rests_on for its place on the fuselage and other_joins for the wedges above it.

The remaining-parts list still shows 1x trans-green and 1x trans-red round plates, but I placed b21 and b22 on page 5. They look like an inventory mismatch (the trans-orange ones were removed instead). I did not place them twice.
Step 9: two light-gray 6x3 wedge plates (right and left) are set across the orange 2x6 plate b23 as the wings. Which wedge is on which side is a guess from the picture.
Step 10 (2x): two orange 2x1 curved bricks sit at the wing root, in line with the fuselage. They clutch the orange plate and a wing each, which is my reading of the picture.

The remaining-parts list on this page still shows the gray wedge plates as unplaced and removes a white 2x6 plate instead. The picture clearly shows the gray wedges, so I placed those. The list looks mismatched.
Step 11: a white 2x6 plate is laid crosswise over both gray wing wedges, making the wing top. The orange curved slopes stay visible beside it, so I did not list them in rests_on.
I assumed it clutches only the two wedges b24 and b25.
Step 12: the black propeller goes on the nose pin of b14 and spins. Two trans-brown cheese slopes (windscreen) sit side by side at the front of the orange 2x4 plate b15.

Step 13: a black 1x2 plate goes on each wing tip, on the white wing plate b28, one near each end. A trans-orange round plate is on each black plate, as the picture shows orange dots. Exact positions are a guess.

The remaining-parts list still shows the trans-green and trans-red round plates, although I placed those as b21 and b22 on page 5. The orange dots here are the trans-orange round plates, and the list had already dropped them. I used the colours shown in the pictures.
This is a new sub-assembly, the first of two floats. It is separate from the plane and the earlier sub-assemblies.
Step 1: the black 1x4 plate is pressed onto the studs of the black curved inverted 4x1 hull piece. The arrow is hard to read, but the curved piece has only studs, so the plate must go on top.
Step 2: a black 1x2 plate with a bar up is pressed onto two studs of the 1x4 plate, bar pointing up. I assumed it lines up with the middle studs, and the plate overhangs one end.
Step 3: a black 1x6 plate is laid across the float at right angles, sticking out sideways. It seems to sit on the studs of the bar-up plate b38, but the picture is not clear.
Step 4: an orange curved 4x1 brick with no studs is pressed onto the studs of the black 1x4 plate and the bar-up plate. This is the orange top of the float.
The bar of b38 still points up beside the orange curved brick.

The boxed steps 1-3 repeat page 10 steps 1-2 and page 11 step 4 for a second float: the curved hull b41, the 1x4 plate b42, the bar-up plate b43 and the orange curved top b44. The second float has no 1x6 plate.

Step 5 joins the two floats. The free end of the 1x6 plate b39 on the first float is pressed onto the second float's plate, so the floats face each other and the bars point up. I recorded this as an other_join because b39 was placed earlier. It may really be a stack with b39 above b42.
The exact overlap and which studs clutch are guesses.
Step 6: a black bar holder with clip is put on the upright bar of each float (b38 and b43). The clips point up.

Step 14: the float assembly is lifted up so the two clips snap onto the silver round plates under the nose. The red arrows point at the nose wheels. I picked one silver plate on each bracket (b9 on b8 and b12 on b11), but could not tell which of the pair is used.
I recorded the bar holders in other_joins because they clip on rather than rest on anything.

Page 14 starts the booklet's second (alternative) model, shown in the preview as a gray-sailed boat/plane. It reuses the same physical bricks as the first model. I gave them new ids (b47 onward) because ids are never reused. This is a separate model, so the first piece b47 has rests_on [].
Step 1: the black curved inverted 4x1 hull piece (b47) is joined with a black 1x6 plate (b48). As in the first model, I took the plate to sit on the hull's studs, at the left end.
Step 2: a black 1x4 plate (b49) is pressed onto the 1x6 plate with two arrows, one per end. I assumed it sits on b48 only, offset from the hull end.
Step 3: the orange curved 4x1 brick with no studs goes on the right end of the black 1x6 plate b48, as the tip of the hull.

Step 4: two white 2x6 plates are set side by side, turned across the base, making a 4-wide deck over the black plates. The picture is not clear about which studs they clutch, so I listed both black plates b48 and b49 for each.
The orange piece is still visible beside the deck, so the deck does not cover it.
This is still the second (alternative) model, separate from the first plane.
This repeats page 14 steps 1-2 to make the second black hull base of the second model, with new ids b53-b55. It is a separate sub-assembly, not yet joined to the first.
Steps 1-2: the curved inverted 4x1 b53 is joined to the black 1x6 plate b54. The black 1x4 plate b55 is then pressed onto b54. The plate/hull stacking order follows my reading of page 14.
Step 3: an orange curved 4x1 brick b56 goes on the right end of the second 1x6 plate b54, the same as b50 on the first hull.
Step 5: the second hull is turned around and pressed onto the other side of the white deck. The two hulls then sit as parallel floats (a catamaran) with the deck between them.
The white deck plates b51 and b52 were placed earlier, so I recorded this join in other_joins. I assumed both deck plates clutch b54 and b55, since the picture does not show exactly which studs.
Boxed sub-assembly: a black 1x2 plate (1) with two trans-brown cheese slopes side by side on it (2) makes the canopy. It is placed on the white deck in the middle, bridging the two white 2x6 plates.
Step 6 picture also shows a trans-green round plate on the left hull b49 and a trans-red round plate on the right hull b55, which were not there on page 17. I took them as added in this step.
Which hull end carries the green and red plates, and the exact stud under each, are my reading of the picture.
This is a new small sub-assembly (see the preview at the top) for the second model. It is separate from the catamaran so far.
Step 1: an orange 2x4 plate. Step 2: a light-gray 1x1 brick with a side stud, at one end, with its side stud pointing outward.
Step 3: the black piece at the left end looks like the 1x2 plate with handles on ends, laid across the plate edge. I am not sure it is that piece.
Step 4: an orange 1x2 plate is pressed on, covering the top stud of the gray brick and one orange plate stud beside it. The two arrows show those two studs.
Step 5: an orange curved 2x1 brick with no studs goes on top of the orange 1x2 plate b65. It covers the gray side-stud brick's top stud, which the picture hides.
Step 6: the sub-assembly is turned around (rotate symbol), so nothing is added.

Step 7: the sub-assembly is placed on the white deck behind the canopy. Its orange plate b62 clutches the deck plates, which were placed earlier, so I recorded the join in other_joins. The exact studs are a guess.
Boxed steps 1-2: a dark-gray bracket gets two flat-silver round plates on its two top studs. I treated them as resting on the bracket, not side joins as on page 3.
Boxed step 3: the bracket is pushed sideways onto a white sloped piece. It looks like the white inverted 3x2 slope with a pin. I used lego-3747b, but this is a guess from the small drawing.
Step 8: the finished piece is placed at the rear of the orange sub-assembly. I assumed the bracket clutches the orange 2x4 plate b62, so the white slope hangs behind it.
The bracket's rests_on and the way it joins the white slope are my reading of the picture.
A new sub-assembly for the second model, shown in the preview as a gray wing with an orange edge. It is separate from the catamaran so far.
Step 1: a light-gray 6x3 wedge plate is pressed on top of an orange 2x6 plate, which the drawing shows as a strip of six studs. The orange plate sticks out beyond the wedge on one side.
I used the Right wedge (54383) and the orange 2x6 plate. The picture does not make clear whether it is the Left or Right wedge, so that is a guess.

Step 3: the wing is turned over (rotate symbol) and two white 3x2 wedge plates (left and right) are pressed on from below, under both the orange plate and the gray wedge. They end up under the wing, so I gave them rests_on [] and recorded the clutch in other_joins.
Step 4: the wing is turned back. A black 1x2 plate with a bar up is pressed on the free orange studs at the right end, bar pointing up. I assumed it rests on the orange plate b71 only.
Several details are guesses from the small drawings: which white wedge goes where, and exactly which studs the black plate takes.
Step 5: an orange 1x3 tile is placed along the edge where the gray wedge meets the orange plate, covering studs of both. This is the second model's fin sub-assembly.

Step 9: the finished fin stands upright and the bar of b75 snaps into the white slope at the back of the deck. The red arrow points at the join. The fin can probably swivel on that bar. I am not sure what the bar fits into, so I used b70, the nearest white piece.
Whether the fin is also resting on anything else is not clear from the drawing.
Page 25 starts the booklet's third model (preview: an orange and white hovercraft or airboat with a propeller). It reuses the same bricks again, so I used new ids from b77.
Step 1: the white inverted 3x2 slope goes on the end of an orange 2x4 plate, the same start as the first model.

Step 2: a dark-gray bracket is placed in front of the slope on the orange plate. Two round studs are on its face. I read them as flat-silver round plates, though they look dark in the picture. I assumed the bracket rests on the orange plate only.
Step 3: one trans-brown cheese slope is pressed onto a stud of the bracket b79, as the windscreen.

Step 4: a black curved inverted 4x1 piece is added. The drawing shows it hovering above with a downward arrow, and another black hull under the model at the bottom. I took it as one piece that ends up as the hull under the orange plate b77. That would put it underneath, so rests_on is [] and I recorded the clutch in other_joins.
This reading is uncertain, because a second curved piece may be added on the other side in a later page.
Step 5: a trans-red and a trans-green round plate sit on the black hull piece b83 (drawn already in place), and a black 1x2 plate is pressed on next to them. All three rest on b83 as I read it.

Step 6 box: the sub-assembly is built 2x. Each has an orange 1x2 plate, a black 1x1 groove tile on it (box step 1), and an orange curved 2x1 brick (box step 2). It is pressed onto the hull at both sides of the bracket. The first copy is b87-b89 and the second copy is b90-b92.
How the tile and the curved brick share one 1x2 plate is a guess from the small drawing. Which hull studs each copy takes is also a guess.
These pieces use up all trans-red and trans-green round plates and the orange 1x2 plates in this model.
A new sub-assembly for the third model (preview: gray wing with two orange pieces on it). It is separate from the hull so far.
Step 1: a light-gray 6x3 wedge plate is placed on a black plate. The black part sticking out looks like a 1x6 plate, along the wedge's long edge.
Step 2: the second 6x3 wedge (the opposite hand) is placed next to the first. Together they make one big triangular wing. I assumed both clutch the black 1x6 plate b93.
Which wedge is Left or Right is a guess.
Step 3: the wing is turned over (rotate symbol), so nothing is added.

Step 4: two white 3x2 wedge plates (left and right) are pressed onto the underside, where the wing's anti-studs face up. They end up under the wing, so I gave them rests_on [] and recorded the clutch in other_joins, as on page 23.
Which wedge clutches which gray wing half is a guess. I listed both gray wedges for each white one.
Step 5: the wing is turned over, then two orange 1x3 tiles are laid side by side on the gray wing, over the join between the two gray wedges.

Step 7: the wing sub-assembly is pressed on top of the hull from page 27. The drawing shows it hovering over the hull. Its underside is the white wedges and black plate, so I recorded the clutch as joins from the white wedges to the hull pieces b86 and b83.
Which exact studs are used, and which white wedge goes on which hull piece, are guesses.
Boxed step 1: two black 1x6 plates are brought side by side. Boxed step 2: an orange 2x6 plate goes on top of them, covering both.
Step 8: the finished block is attached at the front-left edge of the gray wing. I assumed the black plates clutch studs of both gray wedges b94 and b95, but the drawing does not show it clearly.
The black plates could instead be 1x4 plates. I read them as 1x6 from the stud count.
Step 9: a white 1x2 brick is added at the rear corner of the orange 2x6 plate. The picture is small, so which studs it covers is a guess.

Step 10 box: one round plate is pressed onto another, and the pair goes on a free stud of the gray wing near the orange tiles. I used flat-silver round plates, since only they are left in the parts list (the darker colour in the picture may just be shading). I assumed the stud is on b94.
Step 10 also seems to show a small black piece near the orange tiles that I could not identify clearly, so I did not list it. It may already have been there in step 9.

Step 11: an orange curved 4x1 brick with no studs is placed diagonally across the centre of the gray wing, beside the orange tiles. I assumed it clutches wing studs of both gray wedges. The drawing also shows some small black pieces in the centre that I could not pick out clearly, so I added no black piece.

Step 12: a second orange curved 4x1 is lowered with two red arrows. One arrow goes to a stud on the orange plate b102 at the rear, the other to the stacked silver round plates b105. I used those two as rests_on.
The remaining-parts list shows one white 1x2 brick still unplaced, so it probably comes on a later page.
Step 13: a black 1x2 plate with handles on its ends is placed at the rear left, over the orange plate b102, next to the white brick b103. The drawing is small, so that is my reading.

Step 14: the dark-gray 2x2 brick with pin and axle hole goes on top of that plate. Its pin sticks out sideways (the propeller probably goes on it on the next page). I listed the handle plate and the orange plate as what it rests on.

Step 15: an orange piece with studs facing sideways appears beside the dark-gray pin brick. It is hard to identify. I read it as the orange 2x2 plate, resting on the orange plate b102 and standing against the pin brick. This is a guess.
Step 16: the black propeller is pushed onto the pin of b109 and can spin. The model is finished here.
The remaining-parts list still shows one white 1x2 brick unplaced. I could not see it in this page's pictures, so I did not add it. It may be hidden or mis-counted.

Missing white 1x2 brick: the parts list has 2x lego-3004 but I had placed only one (b103). The second one (b112) sits beside b103 on the rear of the orange 2x6 plate b102 in the third model (visible in steps 9-14 as the white block at the rear). Its exact stud position is a guess.

The three separate groups are real, not a mistake. The booklet builds three different models from the same 53 pieces: the seaplane (b1-b46), a catamaran-style boat (b47-b111, first part up to b76 is its wing/fin sub-assembly and hull) and an airboat/hovercraft (b77-b111). Each later model is built after taking the previous one apart. So the pieces of models 2 and 3 are the same physical bricks as model 1, given new ids, and the totals per type are higher than in the parts list.
Because of that, the over-count of lego-3666, 3747b, 18649, 87087, 3022, 99780, 6141, 6232, 3020, 43722, 43723, 3070b, 3795, 54383 and 54384 is expected. I keep all of them and add nothing else.

Within each model the sub-assemblies are joined to the main build (seaplane wing via b23, floats via clips b45 and b46, catamaran wing via b62 and b75, airboat via the joins on pages 30-31). I did not add more edges, as the drawings do not show any further joins.
The missing white 1x2 brick is now fixed: b112 was added in the previous correction, so the lego-3004 count matches the parts list (2).

The 3 separate groups are real. Set 31028 is a 3-in-1: the booklet builds the seaplane (b1-b46), then a second model (b47-b76 and the wing/fin sub-assemblies, a boat with two hulls, b47-b100 range) and a third model (b77-b112), each from the same physical bricks. The models are not meant to be connected to each other.

The extra counts for lego-3666, 3747b, 18649, 87087, 3022, 99780, 6141, 6232, 3020, 43722, 43723, 3070b, 3795, 54383 and 54384 come from this reuse. The same real bricks appear again, with new ids, in models 2 and 3. They are expected, not errors, so I keep every piece.
Inside each model, the sub-assemblies are already joined to their main build, so I add no more edges.
